about: The coverage universe: the normative construct clauses of the adopted SysML v2 and KerML specifications, not the illustrative engineering tables in docs/02-omg-standard-reference.md. `rows` are the matrix rows (the ids the dashboard has always used; they are the aliases that keep the matrix stable). `clauses` names the normative clause behind each row: a stable id, the clause number in the adopted document, and the construct text. A row may rest on several clauses; a row with no normative clause is listed under `unclaused` with the reason, never given an invented clause. Every SysML v2 Part 1 §7 construct clause that has a row of its own is attached to that row (the KerML abstract-syntax row where SysML shares the construct), and each API and Services §7.2 service has a row of its own. A §7 subclause with no row of its own is folded into the row that cites its section (7.5.5 Root Namespaces into TXT:namespaces' 7.5; the action usages 7.17.4–7.17.12 into TXT:actions' 7.17; 7.18.4 Exhibit State Usages into TXT:states' 7.18; 7.21.3 Concern Definitions and Usages into TXT:requirements' 7.21) or is recorded here as a gap rather than given an invented row (7.6.5 Effective Names, 7.6.7 Variations and Variants, 7.6.8 Implicit Specialization, 7.23.3 Trade-Off Analyses); §9 KerML model libraries are the pinned stdlib, recorded as a gap in the KERML entry of `standards`, never invented as rows. Constraint/parametric (CON) rows still come from the class register, docs/CONSTRAINT-CLASSES.md. The standards are the 2026 adoptions named in docs/02-omg-standard-reference.md §1.3, read from /media/sf_Projects/SystemsPerspectiveBib/03_mbse_methods_and_tools/.

clauses.construct: Element — the root of every modeling construct; carries identity, an optional name or short name, and ownership.
Elements — the SysML textual construct for every model element: element IDs and alias IDs, names and short names, and the leading kind keyword (7.2.1 overview).
Relationship — an Element relating a source and a target end; itself an Element, so it can be named, owned and annotated.
Relationships — the SysML textual notation for related elements, owning relationships and the deletion rules they imply.
Dependencies — `dependency from <client> to <supplier>`, a relationship asserting that the client relies on the supplier (7.3.1 overview).
Namespace — an Element that contains members through memberships and exposes them by name; supports name resolution and imports.
Membership — the reified link between a Namespace and a member element, with visibility.
OwningMembership — a Membership that additionally asserts composite ownership of its member.
FeatureMembership — an OwningMembership specialized for a feature: a type owns a feature.
Import — a relationship bringing names from another namespace into scope, public or private.
MembershipImport — an Import of a specific membership from another namespace.
NamespaceImport — an Import of the members of another namespace, recursive where stated (`::**`).
Type — anything that classifies: the abstract supertype of Classifier and Feature, owning features, specializations and multiplicity.
Classifier — a Type that classifies things directly.
Definitions — `<kind> def <name>`: a Classifier declared with a kind keyword, optional `specializes`/`:>` subclassifications, and a namespace body.
Feature — a Type that classifies values in the context of another type; has a featuring type and a type, with ordered multiplicity-bounded values.
Usages — `<kind> <name> : <Type>`: a Feature declared with a kind keyword, a type and an optional body, the reuse pattern of every SysML usage.
Reference usages — a usage declared with no kind keyword (or `ref`), referential by definition.
Feature chains — a dotted path of usages recording the intermediate features, not just a qualified name.
Specialization — the general subsetting relationship: instances of the specific type are a subset of the general type's instances.
Subclassification — a Specialization between classifiers (textual `:>` or `specializes`).
FeatureTyping — relates a Feature to the Type that types it (textual `:`).
Subsetting — a Specialization between features: one feature's values are a subset of another's (textual `:>`).
Redefinition — a Subsetting that replaces an inherited feature, keeping its value set but changing name, type, multiplicity or value (textual `:>>`).
Conjugation — produces a conjugated type with input and output directions reversed (textual `~`).
Multiplicity — a bound on a feature's value count.
MultiplicityRange — the lower and upper bound of a multiplicity (textual `[lo..hi]`, `[n]`, `[*]`).
Class — a Classifier whose instances are identity-bearing objects.
Structure — a Class whose instances are composite structures.
DataType — a Classifier whose instances are pure data values.
Association — a Classifier typed relationship between features.
Connector — a feature whose values are links between its ends; the basis of connections and interfaces.
Behavior — a Class that classifies performances.
Step — a Feature that is a usage of a Behavior.
Function — a Behavior with a result parameter: a value-returning behavior.

Expression — a Step that is computable; its subtypes (8.3.4.8.1–18) include literal, operator, invocation, feature-reference, constructor and collect expressions, the basis of calc and constraint bodies.
Succession — a Connector that orders its ends in time (control flow).
Flow (ItemFlow) — a Step that transfers values or items from one feature to another (object flow); SuccessionFlow (8.3.4.9.6) orders them in time.
Flow definitions and usages — `flow def`, and `flow`/`message`/`succession flow` usages; messages declare their payload with `of`.
Package — a Namespace that owns its members as a library or model package.
Metaclass — a Structure that classifies metadata features.
MetadataFeature — a feature that is a metadata instance of a Metaclass.
Annotation — the reified relationship applying an annotating element to its annotated element.
Annotations — the SysML notation attaching a comment, documentation or textual representation to one or more model elements.
Comment — an annotating element carrying body text for a model element.
Comments — `comment <name> /* … */`, a comment that may be named and is a member of its namespace.
Documentation — a Comment whose body is the documentation of its annotated element.
Documentation — `doc /* … */`, a comment that documents its single owning element.
TextualRepresentation — an annotating element carrying a textual rendering of its annotated element in a stated language.
TextualRepresentation — a textual body in a named language (the `rep` notation) rendered as an annotation of its element.
Namespaces and packages: package definitions and usages, owned members and aliases (7.5.1–7.5.2).
Imports — public/private, membership and namespace (recursive `::**`) imports, with import filtering (7.5.4).
Attributes — attribute definitions (DataTypes) and attribute usages with types and values.
Parts — part definitions and part usages, composite features owned by a definition or usage.
Items — item definitions and item usages: things that flow or are conserved.
Ports — port definitions and usages with direction (`in`/`out`/`inout`) and conjugation (7.12.3).
Connections — connection definitions and usages, bindings as usages, feature values and successions as usages (7.13.2–7.13.5).
Interfaces — interface definitions and usages, the port-to-port connection contract.
Actions — action definitions and usages, parameters, succession shorthands and structured control.
Control nodes — fork, join, merge, decision and the initial/final nodes.
States — state definitions and usages, entry/do/exit behaviors.
Transition usages — trigger, guard and effect between states.
Calculations — calculation definitions and usages with result expressions.
Constraint definitions and usages — a constraint definition is a Predicate; a constraint usage applies it.
Constraint usages — `constraint c : C { … }`, a Boolean expression with owned parameters.
Assert constraint usages — `assert constraint { … }`, a constraint usage that must hold.
Requirements — requirement definitions and usages with subject, require and assume, concerns, and satisfy requirement usages (7.21.4).
Allocations — allocation definitions and usages, the cross-cutting allocate mapping.
Views and viewpoints — view and viewpoint definitions and usages, renderings, compartments and diagrams as view usages (7.26.5).
Enumerations — enumeration definitions and usages with enumeration literals.
Occurrences — occurrence definitions and usages, time slices and snapshots, individual and event occurrences (7.9.3–7.9.5).
Metadata — metadata definitions and usages, semantic metadata and user-defined keywords (7.27.2–7.27.4).
General View (gv) — the default compartment for a package; definitions and usages drawn as nodes and edges.
Interconnection View (iv) — the default compartment for a part: nested parts, their ports and the connections between them.
Action Flow View (afv) — the default compartment for an action: actions, parameters, control nodes and flows.
State Transition View (stv) — the default compartment for a state: states and the transitions between them.
Sequence View (sv) — the default compartment for an occurrence: lifelines and time-ordered event occurrences (9.2.20.2.7).
Requirement view — the GeneralView filter over requirement definitions/usages and satisfy/derive/refine, drawn by the requirements graphical notation.
Cases, analysis cases and verification cases — their graphical notation, including subjects, objectives and results.
Case definitions and usages — `case def`/`case`, a calculation-like construct with a subject parameter, actor parameters and an objective.
Analysis case definitions and usages — `analysis def`/`analysis`, a case whose objective concerns its analysis result.
Verification case definitions and usages — `verification def`/`verification`, a case whose result is a pass/fail/inconclusive/error verdict.
Use case definitions and usages — `use case def`/`use case`, a case with external actors and an include-use-case usage (7.25.3).
Allocations graphical notation — the allocate mappings, typically rendered as a matrix or table.
Browser View (bv) — the ownership/membership hierarchy from an exposed root, rendered as a collapsible tree.
Grid View (grv) — exposed elements and relationships arranged in a rectangular grid; Table 34 names no graphical rendering clause for it.
Geometry View (gev) — a 2D/3D visualization of exposed spatial items; Table 34 names no graphical rendering clause for it.
ProjectService — create, read, update and delete projects.
ProjectDataVersioningService — branches and their lifecycle.
ProjectDataVersioningService — tags and their lifecycle.
ProjectDataVersioningService — commits, the write path for model content.
ElementNavigationService — elements, roots and directional relationships read at a commit.
QueryService — stored queries and query results.
ExternalRelationshipService — create, read and delete the relationships an element has to elements outside the project.
ProjectUsageService — create, read and delete usages of one project's content by another project.

unclaused.note: No normative clause: 02-omg-standard-reference §5.7's "Other" group is the reference server's POST /transform and POST /validate, which the API and Services specification does not define. The row is kept as an existing alias and stays unmeasured; no clause is invented for it.
